result.title: Forecast Value Add: Reward-Based Action Selection over Probabilistic Demand Forecasts
result.summary: Strong machine-learning ensembles capture much of the trend, seasonality, and known events in demand, yet they can still understate peaks, miss moving events, or mistake temporary changes for shifts in demand level. We address this gap by framing forecast refinement as a reward-driven decision problem. For each forecast period, we let an agent choose among values already produced by the ensemble: its base forecast, distribution-free bounds, quantiles, and a bias-corrected estimate. We evaluate these choices against context-matched historical periods, accounting for calendar position, recurring and moving events, trend, price, and promotions. We then apply a structural seasonal guard to constrain adjustments and record the model, agent, and planner contributions to every published value. We evaluate our approach across five retail, consumer-goods, and direct-to-consumer deployments over nine months. Our refined forecasts reduce mean WMAPE by 6.3% compared with the stacked machine-learning forecast for every customer, with gains reaching 16.7%, and achieve the lowest error in 35 of 45 customer-months. Compared with statistical forecasts, our approach reduces mean error by 18.7%. These results demonstrate that context-aware, auditable action selection can add forecast value beyond a strong ensemble.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把需求预测修正表述为奖励驱动的决策问题：对每个预测期，agent 在集成模型已产出的候选值（基预测、无分布区间界、分位、偏差校正值）中选择，用情境匹配的历史期做评估，并施加季节性结构约束、记录模型/agent/规划者各自贡献；在五个零售部署中平均降低 6.3% WMAPE。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但其「在既有候选中按奖励挑选并逐值记录来源贡献」的框架，可能为 LVR 中 latent 候选或假设筛选、以及 THINK/LOOK 收益的贡献分配提供可审计的类比线索，可供核查。
